newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian military slams U.S. human rights report.
newsitem.headline: Colombian military slams U.S. human rights report.

text.p: Colombia's military strongly criticised the United States on Tuesday and flatly rejected a State Department report that linked the Latin American country's army to widespread human rights abuse.

A harshly worded statement by Colombia's top military commanders, led by army forces chief Gen. Harold Bedoya, said the report violated "the dignity and institutional honour" of all those who serve in Colombia's military and contained "a series of baseless accusations."

The State Department report, issued as part of an annual summary of the human rights situation around the globe, quoted what it described as "reliable" non-governmental human rights groups as saying security forces were reponsible for eight percent of the political murders committed in Colombia during the first nine months of last year.

Echoing other reports issued by prestigious groups like London-based Amnesty International and New York-based Human Rights Watch, it also linked the military to numerous cases of torture and to right-wing death squads responsible for most of Colombia's political murders.

"It's difficult to understand how the report can present the security forces as violators of human rights when it is they, precisely, who have unleashed and continue unleashing a huge battle against narco-terrorism," the military heads said.

They added that drugs and the drug trade had "engendered the greatest human rights violations, nationally and internationally, through crime, corruption, drug addiction and the gradual destruction of youth, the environment and world economy."

Military officials could not be reached for immediate comment on the timing of the statement, which came as the military was fighting a fierce battle with Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels on the outskirts of the capital.
